headline: Severe flooding in Chittagong: Banshkhali area submerged for 4 days
summary: Thousands of families are stranded as homes, roads, and farmlands are underwater, causing acute shortages of food and drinking water.
details: Banshkhali, a coastal area of Chittagong, has been completely submerged under floodwaters for four consecutive days, leaving thousands of families stranded.
The flooding has caused widespread devastation, with homes and roads underwater and vast stretches of agricultural land destroyed.
In the Chanuya Union, many mud houses have collapsed under the pressure of the floodwaters, leaving numerous families homeless and forced to seek shelter in higher ground or emergency centers.
The affected population is facing a severe crisis of food and clean drinking water, while several areas remain without electricity.
Agricultural losses are significant, as paddy fields and salt farms have been submerged, and fish from ponds have washed away.
The flooding has heavily impacted multiple unions, including Puichhari, Shekher Khil, Katharia, and Gandamara, where most villages are now underwater.
caption:
Thousands of families are stranded in Chittagong's Banshkhali after 4 days of continuous flooding.

Banshkhali, a coastal area of Chittagong, has been completely submerged under floodwaters for four consecutive days, leaving thousands of families stranded.

The flooding has caused widespread devastation, with homes and roads underwater and vast stretches of agricultural land destroyed.

In the Chanuya Union, many mud houses have collapsed under the pressure of the floodwaters, leaving numerous families homeless and forced to seek shelter in higher ground or emergency centers.

The affected population is facing a severe crisis of food and clean drinking water, while several areas remain without electricity.

Agricultural losses are significant, as paddy fields and salt farms have been submerged, and fish from ponds have washed away.

The flooding has heavily impacted multiple unions, including Puichhari, Shekher Khil, Katharia, and Gandamara, where most villages are now underwater.

headline_marked: Chief Prosecutor says [[people want Sheikh Hasina back in Bangladesh]] as soon as possible
headline: Chief Prosecutor says people want Sheikh Hasina back in Bangladesh as soon as possible
summary: International Crimes Tribunal (ICT) Chief Prosecutor Aminul Islam says there is no place for the former PM and the Awami League in Bangladesh.
details: International Crimes Tribunal (ICT) Chief Prosecutor Aminul Islam stated that the people of Bangladesh want former Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina to return to the country as soon as possible, rather than in December.
The Chief Prosecutor made these remarks on Saturday afternoon at an event organized by the July Martyr Memory Foundation at the Press Club in Dhaka.
His comments come as a reaction to a Reuters report stating that Sheikh Hasina would return to Bangladesh in December to surrender in court.
Aminul Islam emphasized that there is no place for Sheikh Hasina or the Awami League in Bangladesh legally after being ousted from power.
He assured that there is no need to be disappointed regarding the trial of the July martyrs, asserting that every single incident from July will be investigated and tried.
The Chief Prosecutor added that the judicial work of the tribunal is moving forward more rapidly under the current government.
He also urged the public not to spread misinformation or confusion on social media regarding the legal proceedings.
caption:
People want Sheikh Hasina back in Bangladesh immediately, not in December, says the ICT Chief Prosecutor.

International Crimes Tribunal (ICT) Chief Prosecutor Aminul Islam stated that the people of Bangladesh want former Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina to return to the country as soon as possible, rather than in December.

The Chief Prosecutor made these remarks on Saturday afternoon at an event organized by the July Martyr Memory Foundation at the Press Club in Dhaka.

His comments come as a reaction to a Reuters report stating that Sheikh Hasina would return to Bangladesh in December to surrender in court.

Aminul Islam emphasized that there is no place for Sheikh Hasina or the Awami League in Bangladesh legally after being ousted from power.

He assured that there is no need to be disappointed regarding the trial of the July martyrs, asserting that every single incident from July will be investigated and tried.

The Chief Prosecutor added that the judicial work of the tribunal is moving forward more rapidly under the current government.

He also urged the public not to spread misinformation or confusion on social media regarding the legal proceedings.
